title: Bartleby, the Scrivener
author: Herman Melville
summary: A Wall Street lawyer hires a copyist who gradually refuses the work he is asked to do. Melville’s complete 1853 story appears with explanatory notes and material on the offices, institutions and working life behind it.
descriptionParagraphs: The story is arranged in ten editorial reading sections without changing the narrative. Summaries and historical context accompany the text, with explanatory footnotes and critical perspectives.
The supporting material covers legal copying, Wall Street, the Court of Chancery, the Tombs and the Dead Letter Office.

title: Selected War Poems of Wilfred Owen
author: Wilfred Owen
image: Wilfred Owen War Poems Main Cover.png
summary: Twenty-four of Owen’s poems follow the expanded 1921 reprint of Poems, with numbered lines, explanatory footnotes and First World War context.
descriptionParagraphs: The selection follows the 1921 reprint, which expanded the twenty-three poems of the 1920 collection to twenty-four. Notes explain vocabulary, references and the conditions of military service.

The editorial material covers trench warfare, gas, shell shock, Owen’s relationship with Siegfried Sassoon, pararhyme and critical reception. A glossary, critical perspectives and teaching pathways accompany the poems.

Numbered lines and explanatory footnotes
First World War and biographical context
Critical perspectives, glossary and teaching pathways

title: Dubliners
author: James Joyce
summary: Joyce’s fifteen stories of Dublin life are presented in the text of the 1914 first edition, with explanatory notes and a summary and context section after every story.
descriptionParagraphs: This edition includes all fifteen stories, from The Sisters to The Dead. Explanatory footnotes accompany the text, while the supporting material traces the book’s difficult route to publication and its later reception.
The historical material covers Dublin’s streets and institutions, Catholicism, politics, work, emigration, music and language, alongside the stories’ adaptations.

Explanatory footnotes
Publication history, reception and adaptations

title: Pygmalion
author: George Bernard Shaw
summary: Shaw’s complete 1916 Constable text follows Eliza Doolittle’s encounter with the phonetician Henry Higgins. The edition includes the full Preface and What Happened Afterwards, with act summaries, explanatory footnotes and historical context.
descriptionParagraphs: This edition presents the play before the additions made for the 1938 film. Act summaries and contextual notes accompany the complete text, including Shaw’s sequel.
The supporting material covers Shaw’s life, London in 1912, phonetics and class, Covent Garden’s flower trade, censorship, the disputed ending and My Fair Lady.

title: To the Lighthouse
author: Virginia Woolf

Textual history includes the differences between the original British and American editions and the revisions made in later printings.
